text:
Luke Evangelista came to New Jersey after 253 games in Nashville, and the Devils are getting what they wanted from him. With him on the ice at five-on-five they take 60.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), almost six points better than when he sits.

The points have lagged that. He has 12 in 20 games, and four over his last ten when our numbers expected about seven. New Jersey has scored 4.5 fewer goals than expected with him on, which is the main reason. His goal against Montreal was a reminder he can finish, but he is more passer than shooter: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.1 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 89th percentile among forwards, and his closest comparisons are Patrick Kane and teammate Jesper Bratt.

Evolving-Hockey rated him 3.5 wins above replacement in 2025-26, sixth among 401 forwards, though it warned that results ran ahead of his chances. The Toronto native projects to 53 points by our numbers.
headline: Evangelista's new team is winning his minutes
